# GreenDocs Agent Instructions

Before acting, read [agent onboarding](../AGENTIC/README.md), the [product brief](../docs/PRODUCT_BRIEF.md), and the [system architecture](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Read environment, operations, access, security, and domain guidance relevant to the task. Check the current task's acceptance criteria and tracker; do not assume a repository TODO list exists or invent priorities.

Use the configured repository and public site recorded in `AGENTIC/PROJECT_ACCESS.md`. The owner authorizes use of local and GitHub tools actually available in the current environment; an explicit request to commit or push authorizes that requested operation after reviewing the target and staged diff. This does not grant technical capabilities or credentials missing from the active session. Never put PATs, OAuth secrets, or other credentials in documentation, source, tests, logs, command arguments, URLs, commits, or build output. Authentication must use the approved GitHub-only flow; ask the user to enter any needed credential directly into the intended secure UI, never into chat.

Inspect current code and tests before editing. Treat docs as documented intent, verify implemented behavior against code, and report discrepancies. Keep changes focused, update canonical docs when behavior or contracts change, and run the smallest relevant checks. Follow the actual permissions and tools in this session; ask before downloading/installing missing tools. Do not claim an agent, permission, test, browser acceptance, or deployment was available or successful.

When asked to start the local app, run `corepack pnpm@12.11.2 dev` from the workspace root immediately. Do not preflight-check ports, probe the live site, or repeat environment/setup checks; the configured project workspace is ready to run. Use Vite's startup output for the local URL. Open the local and deployed app URLs in the VS Code integrated browser when that tool is available; do not print the URLs in chat unless the user asks or the browser is unavailable. The deployed URL is in `AGENTIC/PROJECT_ACCESS.md`. Diagnose only if startup reports an error, and ask before installing anything.

For requested Git commit/push operations, use the existing workspace Git configuration. Make only a brief readiness check of the current repository, worktree, target branch/remote, and required Git identity; do not reconfigure Git, re-authenticate, or repeat setup when already wired. An explicit user request authorizes the requested commit and/or push. Review and stage only task-related changes, run relevant checks, and proceed; if the target is ambiguous or the configured operation actually fails, stop and report that specific blocker. Never force-push.

Never put PATs, OAuth secrets, or other credentials in docs, source, tests, logs, command arguments, URLs, commits, or build output. Never request credentials in chat; the user must enter them directly into the approved secure UI. Do not commit or push unless the current user request explicitly authorizes it. Before an authorized Git side effect, inspect the target, worktree, staged diff, and relevant checks. Never force-push or write unapproved test data to production.

Consult the read-only Project Architect for architecture explanations or impact traces, and the read-only Backend Planner when planning changes to the protected `/backend` blank-header route. These specialists are optional and never replace checking current docs/code. Use the Documentation Maintenance skill when making a structural documentation change.
